additionality.narrative: VT0008 applied. Step 1 (alternatives) is not applied because AMS-III.AV sets the baseline scenario. Regulatory surplus: no Tanzanian law or regulation requires households in Moshi Rural District to treat drinking water or use filtration devices (Water Supply and Sanitation Act 2019 reviewed). Step 2 barrier analysis: households cannot pay the upfront filter price (about 1.5 months of median rural cash income) and no micro-finance product covers it; carbon revenue funds free distribution and the maintenance network. Step 4 common practice: 2 similar household-filter activities exist in the region (N_all = 2), 1 of them uses an essentially different technology, chlorination tablets (N_diff = 1); F = 1 - N_diff/N_all = 0.5, above 20 %, but N_all - N_diff = 1, not more than 3, so under VT0008 Step 4 the project is not common practice.

summaryDescription.summaryText: The project distributes 3,000 ceramic-membrane point-of-use water filters across four zones of Moshi Rural District, Tanzania, serving approximately 12,000 people. Before the project, households boiled drinking water over three-stone wood fires. The filters remove the need to boil, avoiding non-renewable woody biomass combustion.

baselineScenario.baselineScenario: Continued boiling of drinking water over three-stone open fires using non-renewable woody biomass.
baselineScenario.scenarioJustification: Step 1: identify realistic alternatives - continued boiling, unsubsidised filter purchase, or no treatment. Step 2: barrier analysis - filters unaffordable at household income levels. Step 3: continued boiling is the only plausible baseline.
baselineScenario.stepDemonstration: AMS-III.AV baseline determination applied. JMP data shows 42% improved-source access in the district, placing the project in Case 2.
baselineScenario.keyAssumptionsJustification: Boiling efficiency of 0.15 is the survey-weighted average across three-stone fires. Wood share of 0.85 reflects survey findings. fNRB of 0.62 is the published national default for Tanzania.

baselineReassessment.reassessmentSteps: At each crediting period renewal the baseline will be reassessed using current JMP data and a repeat household survey.
baselineReassessment.policyChangeEvaluation: No national or sectoral policy change during the period affects baseline validity.

baselineScenario.baselineInteractiveEffects: The baseline survey asked which device is used for each weekly drinking-water boil; 12% of boils use an improved cookstove, reflected proportionally in the survey-weighted n_wb of 0.15.

additionalityMethods.additionalityDemonstration: Capital cost per unit exceeds two months of median household income in the district and no financing mechanism exists. Carbon finance is the sole revenue source funding distribution, maintenance and testing.
additionalityMethods.commonPracticeAnalysis: Certified point-of-use water filters are used by under 3% of households in the district.

baselineEmissions.beEquation: BE_y = QPW_y x m x X_boil x SEC x SUM_i BL_fuel,i x ((EF_CO2,i x fNRB,i) + EF_nonCO2,i) x 10^-9 x Adj_LE (VMR0015 Eq.(1)); fNRB = 1 for fossil fuels. SEC = [WH x (T_f - T_i) + 0.01 x WHE] / eta_wb (AMS-III.AV Eq.(4)) or 357.48 / eta_wb (Eq.(5)), as selected in Appendix 2.

projectEmissions.peEquation: PE_y = PE_FF,y + PE_EC,y (AMS-III.AV Eq.(6)). PE_FF,y = FC_i,y x COEF_i,y (CDM TOOL03 Eq.(1)), with COEF = w_C x 44/12 (Option A, mass, Eq.(2)), w_C x rho x 44/12 (Option A, volume, Eq.(3)) or NCV x EF_CO2 (Option B, Eq.(4)). PE_EC,y follows Verra VT0010 v1.1, which replaces CDM TOOL05 for this methodology (VMR0015 s8.2): PE_EC,y = PE_A + PE_B + PE_C, with PE_A = EC_PE,A x EF_A x (1 + TDL_A) (Eq.(5), (7)), EC_PE,B = MIN(EC_Grid ; EG_PBWA / (1 + TDL_B)) (Eq.(9)), PE_B per Eq.(8) and shared plants per Eq.(11), (13), (14). EC is in MWh/yr and EF in t CO2/MWh, so PE is in t CO2/yr.

leakageEmissions.leakageEquation: LE_y = 0 (VMR0015 Sec8.3: non-renewable biomass leakage is folded into BE_y via Adj_LE, not added separately)
leakageEmissions.leakageAssessment: Adj_LE = 0.95 was fixed at validation following the AMS-I.E leakage procedure (AMS-III.AV Section 5.4) and is applied within BE_y as VMR0015 Section 8.3 requires; no separate additive leakage term is calculated (LE_y = 0).

quantification.erEquation: ER_y = BE_y - PE_y - LE_y, floored at zero and gated on the water-quality pass rate (>=90%)
quantification.erSummaryNarrative: Estimated net reductions of approximately 1,667 tCO2e per year, about 8,333 tCO2e over the five-year crediting period.
